We visited 4P’s Pizza at D1Mension Residences, and the food was absolutely awesome and delicious. Unfortunately, there were a couple of things that took away from an otherwise enjoyable dining experience.

While serving the dishes, the staff held the food in their hands while explaining the dishes to us from very close range. Because they were speaking so close to the food, I was concerned about saliva droplets potentially reaching the dishes. I found this quite unpleasant and felt that it could be handled in a more hygienic way.

The toilet was another disappointment. It was quite smelly and did not appear to be very clean or well maintained, which was surprising given the restaurant's overall standard.

The food itself was excellent, but I hope the restaurant will pay more attention to food-handling and hygiene practices. These small details can make a big difference to the overall dining experience.

Food good, service not so much.
Apr 2026 • Solo
Pizza 4ps, why have I been having SO MUCH difficulty giving my money to
Pizza 4ps in just the past week? Please make this make sense. I walk there, quite a distance, about 15 minutes before closing. I am told NO, the kitchen closed at 10:30. Why is that not stated on your web page? If it was, I would have never walked there and would not have a problem with this. 

A few days later I walk to a different location, there are at least two empty tables AND at least four empty seats at the bar, I am told NO, they are reserved. I am there, the people who reserved are not. They don’t want my money, I did not reserve. I wasn’t planning to stay for hours, probably 35 minutes at most. Is the thinking that the people who reserve can not be made wait one minute? Seat me, I will be done shortly and the people who reserved will have a very short wait, if any. 

Tonight at Hanoi Centre I am told I can be seated in 75 minutes. I walk around the building and see 8-10 open tables inside and every one outside was unoccupied. I asked how many tables have to be open for me to get a seat at one? I was asked, do you want a table outside? Why wasn’t that offered when I first got there? A manager was called over and I explained the situation, she seated me immediately inside. How does this restaurant have staff whose reactions are completely opposite of each other in 5 minutes time? Make this make sense. I apologized to the manager for appearing frustrated, she found a simple solution to a problem that shouldn’t have existed. She apologized and offered me a complimentary dessert, when I declined and asked for the check she came back, giving me a 50% discount. I hope her bosses are reading this, she is the type of employee you need to keep, she deserves praise, even some extra financial compensation for doing such a great job. Your business will succeed with her problem solving skill and solutions. Please don’t misunderstand me, I have no pretense to think that I should be given special treatment of any kind but the reactions I got made no sense to me, until this manager did such a wonderful job, I thank her so very much and I will return because of her.

Someday when your business isn’t thriving as much as it is today, you should be happy to have customers like me to patronize your restaurant, even after this poor service.

From stars to stables in just three days
Aug 2025 • Family
Traveling to Vietnam with the family we stayed to have dinner twice at this restaurant. The first night we had a Perfect Processing and the food is really great (including pizza). Having been fine on the return of our tour in Cambodia we decided to return three days later, wanting once again to have an alternative to Vietnamese cuisine. The evening was a nightmare. I state I had booked. They made us sit at the same table as three days earlier, when a waitress showed up that we had not seen before. This started to draw up a waiting list 40 minutes 20 minutes on plate that we were ordering, with a lot of effort considering the bad English of the same we were able to tell her to bring the dishes that branch ready in reasonable terms so that the waiting minutes that the waitress had proposed would have passed in the meantime. Morale arrived all together and after about thirty minutes. Spaghetti pizza and meat that I would share with my son. Of course we ate cold pasta and cold meat. Solicited the waitress this was sent another girl who apologized for all the inconvenience they caused us. Not to mention the air conditioning that both scientists could not regulate. Actually they offered us a dessert to overcome their capacity but we refused because we wanted to leave. That said it's a real shame because in your restaurant you eat really well., but you have to invest in capable staff to avoid a horror night like ours,

Molto buono!
Aug 2025 • Family
We originally went to another 4P’s in HCM but they were fully booked up. The lady at reception was kind enough to find availability at this location so we hopped in a grab and headed over.

We weren’t sure what to expect being a half Italian family who go to Italy at least once a year, but having read the great reviews, were intrigued to what a Vietnamese Italian could offer.

We were pleasantly surprised - the quality of ingredients and execution of the dishes was excellent. We had pizza’s - margherita, spicy shrimp, and salami, and the crab spaghetti. All very good.

The food did take slightly too long to come out but our waitress dealt with it so well that it didn’t matter - you can tell they take service very seriously here. 

Highly recommended!

If you get tired of Vietnamese food, hurry to Pizza 4p's!
Jul 2025 • Solo
I remembered that in Japan, comedian Junji Takada used to go to Vietnam and introduce this restaurant to me, so I made a reservation. It's touching to think that a small pizzeria on Letangton Street, more than a decade ago, has now become a major corporation that has landed back all over Vietnam and eventually Japan.
The dishes that come out in a cozy atmosphere are unmistakably delicious, as everyone raves about.
I was particularly surprised by the clam chowder!
The pizza is of course excellent, but you'll definitely want to try this clam chowder. The harmony of clam and seafood broth and cream was the best, and I thought it was the number one dish I had ever eaten. Stay in a friendly shop forever. If you come to Vietnam again, I'll go!

Lipsmacking good and phenomenal service
Feb 2024 • Friends
We checked the menu online and picked a location close to our hotel, and cancelled our original choice of a rooftop restaurant or bar, for our last night in Vietnam. The outlet we visited was packed to the gills and we then moved to this one. Despite being very very crowded with a one hour waiting, the staff at the earlier outlet were exceptionally helpful and courteous. 

Once we got to our new location, from the very beginning the staff was helpful in accommodating our booking change from 2 guests to 4 and gave us a table as soon as they could and tried to ensure we got seats whilst waiting. 

Every drink / dish we ordered turned out to be exceptional. The servers were very perceptive and understood our requirements and ensured that they clarified about allergens, and to the extent of limitations we may have about other ingredients. It shows the training and culture of the Brand. They also took pains to clarify that some dishes would not suit us or apologise for being sold out! 

The (very common) Mojito, or the Sangrias or even the Whey cider were exceptional to say the least. The cheese platters with the toasted breads, the pizza, the desserts (esp the terrine) were fantastic

Personally, I found it refreshing and surprising that a chain with outlets across countries and cities, was able to rise above mass production and yet retain flavour, presentation as also service. 

Highly recommend this to all visitors to Vietnam (and elsewhere), and especially to vegetarians / vegans for the choices.

A restaurant that really captures the energy of Ho Chi Minh City...the cheese is delicious!
Nov 2023 • Couples
This is my first visit in six years. I heard that this small restaurant on Le Thanh Ton Street will open a new store at Azabudai Hills this month, so I really wanted to go. I made a reservation on their official website, but I was worried because I could only enter a Vietnamese phone number.
I ended up entering some random numbers, and although I didn't receive a confirmation letter, my reservation was properly made.
For Japanese people, the quality of the service, ingredients, and taste are impeccable.
The burrata cheese and prosciutto pizza is especially delicious. They also accept half-and-half orders, so you can enjoy a variety of options.
The tomato pasta sauce is made with plenty of natural cheese, and I thought it was even more delicious than the pasta I had in Italy.
The food was served with a smile and was well-done, so I enjoyed my meal.
I would definitely like to try the new store at Azabudai Hills.

Good food but who do you guys think you are?
Jan 2023
Let me start out by saying the obvious: The food is good, even great at times. The pizzas have great ingredients, the pastas and sides are very well done and overall from a pure dining perspective, its good food. 

The problem arises from their service, the staff, the whole HR system across many chains, most concentrated in HCM and Hanoi. Firstly, they are of the belief that that they're some sort of Michelin dining experience with the extremely rude and dismissive attitude of all staff members if you make the ungodly mistake of walking in versus reserving. Even upon reserving, imagine you having not only to answer to the manager of the counter, confirming twice that if truly is you who was blessed enough to make (and get) the reservation, but there is literally staff on the way from the main door to you table, who will ask whether you truly are the one who has managed to obtain this once in a lifetime opportunity to dine in this god-sent institution. 

As a group of tourists, we had heard a lot about this place. While we hail from India, there are at least 15+ outlets in our country where the food is better. What is extremely off-putting was the pedestal these guys put themselves on. You can see and sense its a systemic issue, not a single person one. 

By putting a stronger engine into an old reliable car, you do not convert it into a Ferrari. The same way, by having your staff and your overall service more adamant, rude and egotistical than some Michelin star restaurants I've been to in France, you do not obtain that status.

Big pass from me. Go get yourself a McDonald's if you're lucky.

In HCM, when you are in need of a short break from phos and bahn mi, a pizza from 4Ps is in order. So say the other reviews on TA and on my little guide map, and so I went. I had the half and half version, along with a mojito, on a typical rainy May weekday evening. 

 I didn't have a reservation but it was early and I managed to have a table for one for about 1 hour. It was fair and ample time for a meal. Service staff was helpful to a solo female diner. 

The pizza was thin crust and baked in the brick oven set in the central kitchen. It was okay for a pizza but I can't honestly say it was divine. I picked the tandoori chicken and the prosciutto with a tiny burrata halves. I finished all of the tandoori chicken but left 2 slices of pizza (the other half). 

Now, the alcoholic mojito at 95k dong, is honestly so watered down and wasn't anything more than a non-refreshing minty soda and it is not recommended at all.

I paid 429 000 dong for my meal.

A fabulous restaurant located just round the corner from Ben Tanh Market - perfect to stop for lunch after a good few hours walking around and bartering in the markets. 
The pizzas are INCREDIBLE. We watched the chefs stone-bake the bases and then pass them through to the kitchen where the toppings are added. 
We ordered what we thought was a side salad for starters but a huge salad bowl came out with fresh leaves and herbs as well as a delicious mustard dressing. We ordered half and half pizzas as we couldnt decide what toppings we wanted. We also added a burata cheese on top and wow - everything was so wonderful and fresh. 
Needless to say we could not finish all our food so had the leftovers for dinner that evening. The pizzas still tasted divine then. 

Absolutely 100% worth a visit for delicious fresh pizzas in HCMC and at such a reasonable price. 
We found that after having delicious Vietnamese food in Hanoi and Hoi An, we had been slightly disappointed by the local Vietnamese food on offer in HCMC so were happy to have something else on our last night in Vietnam.

Pizza 4P’s One of the Seven Wonders of Vietnam
Feb 2019 • Friends
Pizza 4P’s has been one of my all-time favorites in pizza places. It a lovely environment that is spacy and welcoming. The chairs are comfortable and have an appropriate distance between each table. However, if you come in at a common time such as 11-12:00 without a reserved table then you can expect to wait 30 minutes or more. My order was a house made mozzarella Caprese salad, garlic pizza slice, burrata parma ham tomato pizza, fondant chocolate cake. 
The first meal was the Mozzarella Caprese which is a dish made with cheese, tomatoes, basil for garnish and olive oil drizzled. After that came the garlic pizza slice which had a chickpeas dip to die for. The slice was crunchy with bits of parmesan shaved on top of the slice and with parma ham. The next meal was the burrata parma ham tomato pizza with a beautiful presentation. The ingredients on the pizza were paired together flawlessly. After all of this delicious food, the last meal was a fondant chocolate cake which was paired with a cool scoop vanilla ice cream. Overall, In my opinion, Pizza 4ps is a must have when visiting Vietnam because of its variety of food.

You'll Like 4P's Too.
Jan 2019 • Couples
There are lots of fusion cuisine experiments underway in Vietnam's cities. This one succeeds. 4P's ('for peace', get it?) offerings could be described as Italian standards reinterpreted by a talented Japanese chef who is so passionate about using fresh local products that he set up his own cheese-making operation in the central highlands. The cheese tray is really good, too. We sampled also salads and a couple of the pizzas -- nicely presented, tasty and reasonably priced. Must I criticize? Well, the bottom of the thin crust pizza was a bit soggy. 

Young Vietnamese professionals are flocking in large numbers to this fast-growing chain. Foreign visitors will find lots to like at the 4P's restaurants, too. The original 4P's outpost in HCM City's 'Little Japan' is up an alley and around a corner -- persevere! You'll find it if you ask passersby or look it up on your cell phone map-app.

San Antonio, Texas27 contributions

Leave it to the Japanese to Perfect Pizza
Nov 2018 • Friends
I have been to SGN 15+ times over 10+ years and have eaten a lot of good food, and watched the food scene really come up to speed over the last 5 years. One of my VN friends told me about this place and we gave it a go, a real hidden gem up an alley and back into a corner off a main drag (Le Thanh Ton) street in Little Japan area (there are other locations). 

The domed brick ceiling reminded be of underground restaurants in Belgium. The bar was spartain in it's liquor offerings, but after all, you're here for the food. A very simple wine and beer menu is what you're limited to but the food pairs nicely with what wine they do offer. 

All of the cheeses are made in-house on a company owned farm in Vietnam, all the greens are locally grown, and the menu is minimalist but covers all the bases with excellent salads, appetizers, and then pizzas you can make half and half to try multiple offerings. They have vegan offerings.

The pizza crust is crispy, light and thin, there are no dough options. The cheeses are incredible. The appetizers - more more more!!!

Highly recommend you make a reservation as this place is packed EVERY night of the week. Walk-ins are generally seated at the bar - wait times commensurate with arrival times.

Magic by Chef Takuto Nakamura, even the Pizza's tastes Michelin Star...
Jun 2018 • Solo
Its like Japanese, Vietnamese and many international flavours beautifully crafted with training from France giving a new meaning to Raffaele Esposit's (Neapolitan pizzamaker) "Pizza Margherita".
The Pizza base is light and well stretched. You might taste the oil if you order the Cheese Pizza that comes with 3, 4 or 5 Cheese (House made Cheese) base. I ordered half and Half - "Teriyaki Chicken" and "Japanese Ginger Pork".First Bite into the Pizza, and it delivers the well marinated Pork and Chicken with flavours oozing out right on my Palate. The Pizza base is not soggy neither dry, its just perfectly cooked and toppings are well distributed so you get the taste in every bite. I savoured every bite of my Pizza and kept thinking of other chef's creations. 
Menu is quite well planned as there is quite a few selection for vegetarians as well. There is quite a vast selection of dishes from Salads, Soups, appetisers and Pastas but Pizza's are their speciality. The items are very well priced for the quality of ingredients used. Service was good and waitstaff was very polite and attentive even at the end of closing of the restaurant.
If you want the first hand experience then you should book the table right next to the Oven where cooks are hand tossing and preparing the Pizza right in front of you. They have 4 convenient Locations to choose from In Saigon. Highly Recommended....

4'P really make me feel like " for peace"
Feb 2018 • Family
I had the chance to eat at 4'P's in District 7 and Ben Thanh Market and it was my first time eating pizza in a different way than the "fast food" I used to call. 
Pizza at 4P's is baked in wood in terracotta oven, in this way the pizza will ripen in just 90 seconds. In particular, the pizza flour must be manually kneaded, the new shell can reach the desired thickness. The base of the pizza is thin, soft but spongy, when biting in you will feel a bit tough, but the smell of powder and smoke smell wood and I can see a lot of scorching scraps on the pizza. That’s the first time I've enjoyed a classic Italian pizza style and it's really different from the pizza we call “ fast food”.

Thanks to 4P's, people knew more about how delicious pizza can be baked. And it was the first time I could have eaten just watching the chefs prepare the pizza and how to cook it. That made me excited when the cook finished a pizza, I was curious whether it was my own or not. For the first time I found the wait so interesting. It gives me a sense of excitement, joy and happiness waiting. And while I was waiting for my pizza to come out, I could sit and watch everything in the restaurant, feeling like I was living a little slow in the midst of the bustling life out there. I like the way the restaurant staff smiled back at me when I looked up at them. Employees always pay attention to each customer's table to see what has been done and clean the dish for neatly, as well as inquiring about what customers are waiting for the next order and order. Any more dishes. The kindness and professionalism of the staff here makes me feel comfortable while enjoying food at here.

World Class Pizza
Apr 2018 • Couples
My wife and I visited Pizza 4P’s as a break from Vietnamese food, thinking that pizza in Vietnam was blatantly catered to tourists – we were so wrong. This is world class pizza by any standards, in London I’ve only eaten pizza this good once or twice. The restaurant itself is in a great location, and is really well laid out. In the centre of the place are two large open ovens where you can watch the chefs put these unique combinations together.

Yes, you can eat a Margherita, but it would be a shame to miss out on their more unique flavour combos. Teriyaki chicken and seaweed, or tandoori, or eggplant. 

This is one of those places where if it were in London there would be a month long waiting list, and the prices would be 5 times higher.

My only tip: For groups of 3+ you will need to book. We only had to wait 15 minutes as a couple, but the group of 4 in front of us had to wait for over an hour.

Potentially The Best Pizza in HCMC
Mar 2018 • Solo
As a pizza lover and no matter where I am in the world, I love to try the local pizza joints. I asked some expats who live in HCMC and Pizza 4P's came up time and time again.

I arrived just after midday and the place was very busy, I was eating alone and they seemed to struggle to process that I wanted a table, yes just for me! Anyway after that things got markedly better, the service was just fine and the food absolutely delicious.

Make no bones about it, if you are looking for "bang-for-your-buck" pizza, this is not the place for you. In relative local terms it's pretty pricey - however I felt it was very tasty.

I opted for 2x starters, I had the ricotta cheese wrap in parma ham and leaves - really delicious/, I also had the garlic pizza slice with chickpea dip - both really nice and the one complaint here is that they didn't arrive together and possibly like a 10 minute between each starter.

For main I had the 4-cheese pizza, really lovely and melt in the mouth cheese - plenty of it ;)

There is also an extensive drinks menu, consisting of; wine, beer, cocktails and soft drinks.

A good place to visit for pizza lovers, however not if you want a cheap bite in HCMC.

BEST PIZZA EVER!
Feb 2018 • Family
We decided to visit this restaurant as it was rated the best pizza in Ho Chi Minh, and with good reason!

When we first arrived, we did not have a booking. They said it would be a 15 minute wait and were very apologetic. We were happy to wait expecting to stand. But they sat us at a table outside with free champaign each while we waited! We were seated within only 10 minutes.

The menu was incredible. Entrees availabke looked amazing and we were not expecting the choices. We had the cheese fondue and garlic pizza. But their were vietnamese style foods were available. They have around a dozen different pizza options, all very different in style. Something for everyone. Vietnamese style and italian style. The pizza bases were one of the best we have ever tried, as shown in the picture. We were a bit hesitant abiut the soy beef pizza but as it was a best seller we got one, IT IS A MUST TRY. Somehow it really works on a pizza.

As for the price, for cocktails and drinks, entrees and 5 pizzas, we only only paid the equivalent of $100 AUD. Very cheap for tge quality of food and how much we ordered between 6 people. They gave us a takeaway box for the leftover pizza.

My name is Natsu, Restaurant manager of Pizza 4P's Hai Ba Trung store
Thank you very much for dining at our restaurant and giving us your honest feedback.

I made a notice about the parking fee in front of the restaurant today.

Out of this world ginger mojitos & pizza
Nov 2017 • Couples
Famous in Saigon they have 3 locations. I can honestly say I’ve never had pizza like this - a Japanese Fusion the bases are so thin with a great crust, 1/2 and 1/2 options - but you have to try their famous cheese pizza. You get a choice of 3 - 5 toppings - cheeses are mage in Dalat, served with drizzled honey as a side. Yes - it’s like nothing else. Service is spot on, ambience great. Best of all - order a ginger mojito or ginger soft drink. Made fresh w homemade ginger and cinnamon syrup and you will never look at a mojito the same way again. Order the non alcoholic version and you have soda plus 2 vials of ginger and sugar to flavour it, of course w mint and lime. I’m going home to google their recipes to recreate. Also offer hand made pastas & gnocchi’s w slow cooked meats and a plethora of other things that I didn’t even look at once I saw the cheese pizza page. As this pizza joint has been highly recommended on Trip Advisor we decided to visit last night- the place was walking distance from our hotel (Sofitel) and was relatively easy to find via google maps.

We made a booking but for 5:30pm so the restaurant was very empty and probably could of just walked in.

The drinks menu was quite extensive and the Sangria I got was delicious however my husband thought his beer was a bit flat.

We got the suggested half and half pizza of margarita and teriyaki chicken- the base of the pizza was thin crust and so good and the toppings on both pizzas were generous and fresh.

I enjoyed the layout of the shop the most- it was set up that you were eating within a "wood-fire oven" with the brick exposed walls.

reviews.review_text:
thaouyen
Sydney, Australia61 contributions
0
Lots of unique and wacky pizzas
Aug 2017 • Friends
A group of 5 friends and I had an enjoyable dinner here last month. We didn't realise that this place was so popular that it needed a booking, but our hotel managed to get us a late seating in a private room. 

From where our taxi driver dropped us off, getting to 4P's requires you to pick your way through a busy alley of restaurants. We were early so we were seated outside and offered a complimentary glass of sparkling wine. 

Inside, the restaurant was busy but our room was private and cosy. The staff spoke reasonable English but require more training. For instance, one of the guests spoke Vietnamese and requested that all alcoholic beverages be put on a separate bill (the host had religious reasons and the rest of us were happy to pay for our own drinks). The staff agreed to do this, but when the bill came out, all the drinks were included. The host paid for it before we knew of the issue, but it was a very uncomfortable moment for everyone. 

As for the food, it was truly exceptional with a big focus on quality ingredients. The menu is quite extensive and would satisfy the most picky eater. The pizza selection has some very weird combinations but all the pizzas we had were delicious. We ordered olives, a cheese platter, salads, 2 pastas, lasagne, 3 pizzas and dessert. I would recommend the cheese platter just to eat the truffle cheese. Delicious.

If you are a pizza purist, this is not the place to go, but if you're desperate for some quality pizza and have the cash to burn, 4P's will more than adequately satisfy your hunger.

Excellent Service...almost over the top
Jul 2017 • Friends
This place has great food. In fact excellent food. The atmosphere is lovely. I was almost going to award this place 3 stars but that's a bit too harsh. We felt rushed. We made a booking at 5pm. After work we managed to all arrive by 6pm some of us had arrived at 5pm only for the server to keep telling us every 5 minutes that we had to leave at 7pm. But the food came out quick, hot and very tasty. What was weird is the way the waitress had this ear piece and walkie-talkie device to put the order through to the kitchen, which we sat next too. It's difficult to write in words what we saw, but imagine the person takes your order and you assume that she would bustle away to get the drinks and appetizers. But instead she stands by the table and repeats your order to who ever is on the other end of the communication device. You can imagine that things get lost in translation so she must have said it about 3 or 4 times. I am just looking at her thinking it would be quicker for her to just tell the kitchen...but persistent paid off despite the place being not big. I also felt like I was 6 years old and my mother was standing over me. The serving staff just stand by the table. And any dirty plate is promptly removed. I am the first to complain about bad service but the amount of staff buzzing around was too much. They were not invisible. The food is good. The service is excellent. Just wish we could have been left to enjoy the food. The company have expanded and I am not sure if this is a good thing. This is the first time I have been here since I arrived in 2009. It's always been difficult to get a reservation and that's what makes it special. I hope the expansion pays off because the product is good.

I might never come back to Le Thanh Ton branch
Jul 2017 • Family
It's sad to say that I've been a loyal of the resto and today was a total let down for me due to the customer service. 

We booked our table for 2 at 6:30PM, and since it was raining that we might not be able to turn up on time. We called the restaurant saying that we would be there at 7PM. Technically, the booking policy can reserve your seats for just half an hour and after that if you cannot make it without prior notice, your booking will be automatically cancelled. We at least made the call to the restaurant that we would be late and we were excited about our dinner, but then a male staff picked up the phone and he sounded unwilling and hesitated to help us out the situation, at least for me. We told him we'd arrive at 7, which made sense because it was meant to be at 6:30 and due to the weather, we tried to arrive at 7 to fit the 30 mins reservation policy. But no, he kept us waiting on the phone for so long and he just went back and forth in and out the resto for about 2 times saying that "Let me go check within the restaurant to see if it's alright for you to arrive at 7, and you have to leave at 8:30 due to another reservation". Seriously, we called and we made a prior notice to arrive at 7, hasn't he learnt the policy? And it sounded like we were being shooed out of place. At least we called, but he sounded off to us, as if we were unreliable or something. I then decided to cancel the booking, just simply because he was not attentive to our request. I'm so fed up. I'd love to come back again but thanks to this, I might not. I understand that this restaurant is on high demand in terms of customers but please, I don't want to see this happen ever again in the nearest future. 

Please train your staff well, today was a disappointment.

4P's is a very famous Pizza place in in town and RESERVATION is a must. It is famous because of it Japanese chef/owner which has put a twist of Japanese finer details onto every dishes; especially, the fresh cheeses that he has made on the daily basic together with fresh and fine ingredients. 

Many Japanese and Foreigners goes here.

It is located at the end of an alley and you cannot miss it because there are always people puzzling on the outside waiting for seats.

The ambient soft but I think the lighting wasn't meant to show off the colorfulness of the foods. So don't be disappointed when the color of your foods not reflected those in the menu.

The foods. Yummmmm.. that's all I can say for the salads, pizzas, spaghettis, and desserts that we had (see photos). Please note that the pizza is about 8" in size and perfect for an individual. 

The price. For all the foods and drinks we had the the bill came out to be about 1.5 million VND which is about $66 usd, which is cheap in my opinion. 

Well, please find this place and enjoy the Japanese twist on the fine Italian foods.

Enjoy and Safe traveling 😉

reviews.review_text:
zangisaac
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam211 contributions
0
Most decent pizza restaurant I've been to
Apr 2017 • Friends
This is my favorite pizza restaurant that I always want to go to or suggest to my friends/relatives. The founders are Japanese so most dishes or pizzas are adjusted with Japanese style, which makes the cuisine much unique. Especially, to the best of my knowledge, all ingredients are directly imported from Japan so you may hardly find any similar style throughout Vietnam. My best choices are: Chicken Teriyaki Pizza, Burrata Prosciutto Margherita Pizza, Calm and the crab spaghetti. I usually do not order appetizers, since a half-half pizza, a salad and spaghetti is perhaps enough for two. As for drink, the restaurant is famous for the so-called "Ginger Ael" which consists of ginger extract, soda and sugar. This is also my favorite drink. Remarkably, the atmosphere of the restaurant is truly awesome! In Le Thanh Ton branch, they will offer you the seats near the stove - where you can watch how the pizzas are made and enjoy your meal at one. However this branch is a little small and sometimes, it makes you feel uncomfortable if you wish to have a silent space. In Southern Saigon branch, the restaurant is much cooler with a lot of tables and two spacious floors. The price is a little bit high for locals, but 200,000VND/person for a decent meal, however, I think, it is reasonable for a weekend hangout. There is some advice:

+ If you want to have the meal here during rush hours (lunch time or dinner time or weekends) or go in group of more than 3 people, you should book the table in advance. In case you come to the restaurant without reservation and if they announce that there are no tables left, normally they will give you and your accompanied two free beverage vouchers for your next visit. If you wish to sit in front of the stove, remember to tell the staff when you make reservation. On some rainy days, when I decided to stop by and have meal here, the staff was so considerate that they offered me an umbrella and towels when they saw my getting wet. This is how I highly appreciate they way they make their service. 
+ The atmosphere is suitable for both friendly handout or formal meeting. If you need private room for business meeting or networking, don't forget to tell them in advance.
+ All the waiters are very active and hospitable. They are good English speakers (but no Japanese).
+ There will be a parking fee in Le Thanh Ton branch. But I think it's free in Southern Saigon if you don't ask the motorbike keepers. Because the keeper remained silent about the fee until I asked him. I think, the restaurant should consider eradicating the parking fee.
+ Finally, I have to say that my suggestions and reviews here are based on my personal experience and my taste. Sometimes, it depends on your taste or which dish do you choose. Some of my friends do not know how to select good meal so they do not think this is a good restaurant. Anyway, Pizza 4Ps will always serve the best part in my heart. May I also say, Saigonese culture has become more meaningful to have a cultural-adjusted culinary corner like 4Ps. Love it!

Delicious pizza in Vietnam!
Feb 2017 • Couples
I am a lover of pizza and when I found that there was a pizza restaurant with excellent reviews literally across the street from our hotel that also served craft beer, I knew we had to make reservations! I must admit that I felt a bit guilty making a booking at a pizza place while in Vietnam, but after a week plus of Vietnamese food (which had been great) we were ready for a break from spring rolls and noodles. We had reservations at 7pm at the Ben Thanh Market location and note that the restaurant is actually a couple doors down from the Market, not in the Market as we originally thought. We were led upstairs and sat at a table right next to the open air kitchen where you could watched all the food being prepared and cooked in the ovens. We were famished and so we ordered two appetizers - the garlic bread with chickpea spread and the ham-wrapped mango. Both of these melted in our mouths! We opted to split a half-and-half pizza - one half the salami and chorizo and the other half the margarita ham with small burrata. The pizza was SO nice and crispy and wonderful. We capped off the evening with an iced coffee for me and camembert ice cream for my husband. We also enjoyed the local craft beer that was on the menu - we were impressed with both of our beers. We were thrilled with the food at 4Ps Pizza and highly recommend a visit while in town!

reviews.review_text:
akostich_11
Los Angeles, California623 contributions

Great Gourmet Pizza after 2 weeks of Vietnamese food!
Jan 2017 • Friends
Coming from LA for a two-week tour of Vietnam, the last thing I expected to be eating would be pizza. With renowned pizzerias like Mozza and Jon & Vinny's in Los Angeles, it would be a waste of an evening to eat pizza in Vietnam where the local food is so well-loved and respected.

That said, after 2 weeks of rice, spring rolls, fish and chicken (among many other local delicacies), it was actually a welcome change to discover such good pizza at the end of such a great trip.

Honestly, the quality of the food here was on par with the best pizzerias that LA has to offer; the dough was soft on the inside but crispy around the crust and bottom-and the ingredients were exciting and unusual! While you could get the traditional (albeit farm-to-table) gourmet toppings like smoked salmon, prosciutto, mushrooms etc., the more adventurous diners could opt for seaweed and calamari and (my personal favorite) burrata cheese.

This hip, fun establishment is a great place to go for a night out; they have beer from the local Heart of Darkness brewery and the vibe is energetic and comfortably noisy with good lighting and ventilation. It's nice to see the brick ovens, which resemble miniature versions of the brick-making ovens we saw early on the tour in the Mekong district.

Highly recommend this place, but only if you've had enough Vietnamese food and are looking for a chance to mix it up!

Good spot if you are looking for pizza with a little twist in HCMC
Dec 2016 • Friends
Great restaurant offering a very nice menu with plenty of choices.
We had couple of appertizers, a salad and 2 pizzas. Everything looked freshly prepared and flavorful. Portions were more than okay.
I've been happily surprised by the "green salad", coming in a large salad bowl with lot of herbs, Iceberg, Lettuce, Red Oak. In most restaurant a green salad is just what it says. But here that was really something else! The owner/chef seems to enjoy giving his own turn on recipes/dishes and it's cool because it's adding a great amount of personality to the food on offer.
Pizzas were definitely the highlight, with somewhat with some twist coming from Japanese cuisine. I have tried a pizza topped with "Gyu Don" that was quite interesting! The other one was a bit more generic but did a very good job at filling my tummy and was okay to my tastebuds!
You can also choose to half/half the pizzas, that's another plus.
Food came fast, in reasonable portions and was tasty. 
Definitely a place to stop by when you hit HCMC!
I will consider going there again during my next trip Vietnam, they do have 4 branches (two in Hanoi and two in HCMC)

Foodie heaven
Dec 2016 • Family
I have been going to 4P since they had only 4 or 5 small tables in 2011 and have watched their growth and success with admiration and pride. 

They have grown to 4 restaurants, but they have not sacrificed quality of food or innovative and interesting dishes. AND their service standards are just wonderful. Not only are there staff well trained and attentive, but they all seem to stay a long time, which can only mean that Mr. Masuko si a great owner to work for. 

As for food- their burrata cheese and cheeses are well known among food cognoscenti in Vietnam. All homemade and delicious, so naturally their pizzas are interesting and tasty. But their salads are delicious with quality tasty and fresh greens, their pastas are all great AND their lemon tart desert is the closest thing I can find to my grandmothers lemon meringue recipe that she brought to heaven with her.

Oh, and their local craft beer menu is fantastic as you cannot find many places that offer a selection from 5 or 6 local beer makers...

Sep 2016 • Couples
Pizza 4P's is a good place for dates or big groups of friends for special occasions. It's pricey, so it's a once in a while thing, but it's delicious. It's very popular now, so you'll need a reservation at either location, even on a weekday. We have sometimes managed a bar seat with just two of us. Only place I've ever had salmon sashimi pizza. Wouldn't normally try such a thing, but it's really good and we get it each time we go now! The burrata. yum. The Ricotta Cheese Wrapped with Parma Ham is a delicious and fun appetizer. The d7 location is hard to find. It's behind fv hospital and an auto dealership. The roads leading up to it have been ripped up recently so be careful and maybe don't take a motorbike there, as I found it hard and unsafe to drive on. There's a good parking lot next door. Pizza 4P's in d7 has the ambiance of a warehouse restaurant in Brooklyn. The one in d1 has a comfier, more hovel-like feel with the decor of the ovens about. Upstairs has a bit of an artsy, library feel. I definitely recommend it. One of the highlights of HCMC.

Salmon Sashimi Pizza a MUST TRY!!!!!
Feb 2016 • Friends
When a local Vietnamese friend first brought me to 4P's for pizza a few years ago, I had my reservations. I mean, come on, one would go to Vietnam to eat pho or Vietnamese springrolls. One would go to Beijing to savour the Peking Duck. Japan for sushi. You get my point. Pizza in Vietnam just does not match. But was I ever so wrong!! Hidden at the end of a back alley, this restaurant freshly bakes amazing pizza. The best I have ever tasted. Especially the salmon sashimi pizza is TO DIE FOR!!! Just writing about it now is making my salivate ~

After my first visit, I did my online research on the restaurant. It was opened by Japanese. No wonder the unique combination of salmon sashimi with pizza. Please don't be mistaken, the restaurant serves all the other usual pizzas too which tastes wonderful as well. I mention the salmon sashimi pizza because it is such an ingeniously blended taste of heavenly culinary fusion. The Japanese always have a way of refining foods. Just like the Japanese curry which has a more refined smooth taste than the Indian curry. And it is in this light that 4P's has refined the pizza too. 

Ever since, this has been my must go to restaurant every time I visit Saigon. And it is packed. You MUST make a reservation days in advance to get a table!! Yes, it is that good. reviews.review_text:
Kevin S
4 contributions
0
How is this place rated so high? Mistakes and lies
Aug 2016 • Couples
I finally decided to try out the well known 4P's pizza. Reserving a table for two at the early and non crowded time of 6:30 pm. We sit down and order two 10" pizzas, the small german potato appetizer, and two cokes. Price 832.000 vnd. 
We had a choice to have the pizzas come out together or separately. Since we were sharing and didn't want cold pizza. We chose separate. Biggest mistake of the night. 
The Coca Colas come out first. They offer to open them, offer accepted. So far, so good. 
The German potato appetizer comes out next. 55.000 vnd. Definitely a small size for sure. Maybe one small sliced red potato. But ok flavor. Nothing special. Wouldn't order it again.
Next a few minutes after the plate is cleared, our first pizza comes out. Half 4 cheese and half soy beef. I think the price was 200.000. Both were average to slightly above average taste. I visit Buzza pizza frequently and the taste of the ingredients is very similar to Buzza pizza and I get that pizza for 75.000 vnd with membership card and it's bigger. ... Here is where the trouble started...
They clear our plates and give us clean ones again. Standard service to be expected from an overpriced restaurant. I expect a few minutes wait between pizza's. About 3 or 4 minutes goes by and a pasta comes out. We shake our head and say wrong table. They bring it to the table behind ours. Well, now I think they start our pizza. A few minutes later, a server comes by to apologize about the wait and say it will be out in about 3 minutes. About 10 - 15 minutes goes by and here comes our pizza. They put it down on the table, it's the same pizza we just finished eating. They made us another one. We are waiting on a prosciutto pizza with the mozzarella ball in the middle. 
3 minutes later, a server comes by to apologize and explain that the restaurant is very busy and that's why the order for messed up. She said the food will be out in 3 minutes. 15 minutes later. We finally set eyes on our pizza. I'd estimate about 35 to 40 minutes after we finished our other pizza.
We eat it. My date didn't really like it that much and I didn't think it was worth the nearly 500.000 vnd when u factor in VAT. 
Finished, they take it away and I ask for the bill. I wanted to complain so bad but I worked in the service industry for many years and understand mistakes happen. I don't want to be forced to complain in order to get something for free, but the right thing would have been to give us the pizza for free. Or at least the sodas or the VAT or something. Please don't force me to complain , especially in front of a date at a nice restaurant. 
I pay the bill. While I'm waiting for my change back, one server brings us out two little tiny scoops of ice cream or yogurt or I don't know. It came with another apology. It had no flavor and had frozen ice crystals in the middle of it. Pretty crappy. On top of that, they cleaned our table before they put the ice cream down and wiped it with a rag. The rag was definitely used way too much and left a strong terrible wet rag smell on the table as we ate our flavorless ice cream or whatever it was. The taste was now what we were smelling and it was just a bad end to a bad meal. 
We finish, talk a bit and are still waiting for my change. 
I think they were deciding if they were going to give me the pizza for free but probably decided that since I didn't complain , that they got away with it and I will pay the full bill. 
10 to 15 minutes after paying, the manager comes over and apologized about the wait. She was apologizing about the wait for the money. I count my money, have a few last words with my date and we both stand to leave. The manager then comes over again and apologized two times about the wait for our food and the mistakes. I nod and walk away. 
They were forcing me to complain. A place like this that brings in so much money and holds themselves to a high level of service should respect their name and their customers time and money and should have done more than give us some ice cream they found in the back of the freezer. Especially when there are delicious looking desserts on the menu.
I've been to Buzza Pizza about 40 times and never had a problem. The service is great but not set up as a fancy pants restaurant like 4P's is. Doing the math. I could have went to Buzza about 5 times for the same price as I paid for this terrible experience.
Overall. Mediocre food. Especially for the price. And after getting a good 6 or so apologies without even complaining once. They should have done the right thing and offered the pizza for free and a gift card so I come back another time so they have the opportunity to show me a better experience.
First and last time at 4P's. A waste of my night. A nearly 2 1/2 hour waste of time.
I will be and have been sharing the story with people i know and maybe next time they will learn. If you mess up and mess up and mess up again. Please don't make the customer complain. Do what you know is right for a high level restaurant. Very poorly done on so many levels. You have my money already but now you hear my complaint.

Food amazing but wait times is reason for 4*s instead of 5*s
Aug 2016 • Couples
We first discovered 4Ps in Hanoi and loved it, so we thought we'd try the HCMC one.

It is very difficult to find with no sign from the main Street. You have to turn down a little side road off Le Thanh Ton and it is right at the end of the street. 

We didn't book and turned up around 7.50pm on a Thursday to be told to come back in 30-45mins for a table. We found a little coffee shop nearby and got a smoothie to kill the time. We returned around 35mins later and a table was available as promised which was great.

We orders drinks and food at the same time. The starter came but we were still waiting on the drinks. After what we thought was a reasonable amount of time we reminded the waitress of our drinks. Sadly the starter was finished before the drinks were brought out. 

My pizza came out first - half calamari and half salami. The waitress encouraged us to have half and half on ours pizzas so we could try more which was a great idea. 

However I had already eaten more than half of my pizza before the time my husband's pizza was brought out which was disappointing.

Despite the waiting times the pizzas were delicious and well worth the wait - some of the best pizzas we've had! It's just a shame not to be able to give 4Ps 5*s. 

We also were sat in the outside area upstairs which could do with some additional decoration to make it a bit more attractive - the inside has a lot of character but the outside could do with something more.

Overall though would still recommend and would eat here again - I hope that we were just unlucky with the wait times.

reviews.review_text:
Khoa P
Chicago, Illinois48 contributions
0
Need I say more?
Jul 2016 • Friends
There have been enough reviews on this place already, but why not another one? 
This is a favorite for locals and expats here, in a small alleyway in the Japantown area of D1. DEFINITELY reserve a table, probably 2-3 days before if not more! 
I've tried most of the pizzas here, but my favorite is the duck apple pizza - oh man, the flavors are just perfect! The prosciutto margarita is another favorite of mine - the buratta cheese here is to die for (although some of my friends think it's a bit overwhelming - personal taste I guess). The spicy seafood pizza and salmon miso pizza are also awesome. The salmon sashimi pizza and mayo shrimp are good - but not as good as the other ones. The best part is that they cut up the pizza based on how many people are eating - no more fighting for that one extra piece! 
The salads here are also super fresh. I haven't tried the pastas yet but I've heard great things about them (esp. the tomato one with crab). 
And don't forget dessert!!! I would honestly just go here for dessert if I can - the chocolate fondant, cheesecake, sakura cake and sorbet are all top notch! SOOOOO GOOD! 
Service is also friendly, sweet and professional. 
Can't recommend this place enough, oh man.

My wife, myself and our 17yo daughter have just returned from having dinner at Pizza 4P's (7 July 2016). We decided to give it a go after reading Trip Advisor reviews.

It is a little difficult to find as it's located down a laneway off Le Thanh Ton. The easiest was to find the laneway is it's near the Silverland Sayko Hotel. We walked off the street at about 6pm and was asked if we had a booking. Lucky for us they squeezed us in. 

We had had the spaghetti bolognese and shared a three cheese pizza. Although the pasta was nice it's a little sparing compared to what we get back home in Australia, hence the good decision to get the pizza as well. The pizza was nice as well.

Service was good although one of the waiters knocked a glass off our table, smashing on the floor. The staff were so apologetic. 

For the three of us it cost 740,000 VND, approximately $45 AUD. This was for the food, two waters and a Saigon special beer.

This was one the dearer feeds we've had in Vietnam but the food is nice.

Good food, doubtful otherwise. We were early, so were given seats near the bar to wait; however, there was a strong, toxic, acidic smell of what may have been an adhesive in that area, so we went outside. At the bar I had seen Pasteur Street beer on tap, so when we sat down, I asked for a glass. However, the waiter couldn't find it on his Ipad and I couldn't find it on the drinks menu, so I settled for a glass of Rose wine; unfortunately, when it came it wasn't chilled.

The food was, however, quite good. We wanted just vinegar and oil on our salad, but they don't seem to have it, but the honey-mustard was fine. Excellent tomato soup, excellent lasagna, excellent spaghetti They only have one size pizza, very thin crust, on the small size but enough for two if you have something with it. Our salami and chorizo topping was excellent. Dessert was satisfactory tiramasu, and a small very tasty pudding. I had the cheesecake, which probably would have been very good if half of it hadn't been frozen. My espresso was taken to another table, apparently, so I had to order it again.

The place is noisy - we could hear conversations two tables away. I guess this is because the walls are lined in stone, which is very attractive, but maybe not practical for a restaurant.

The wait staff seemed to be untrained students, working there for the summer; maybe there just wasn't a manager present that evening.

I'd go back to Pizza 4P if somebody else wanted to go, because the food is very good, but I wouldn't suggest it myself.

Having read the great reviews about this place I was very much looking forward to having some good western food. Having been in SE Asia for 2 months and on a budget, my girlfriend and I decided to treat ourselves. Now compared to home this place is still really cheap but compared to the rest of SE Asia it is a little on the expensive side (but worth it!). 

The pizza itself is certainly one of the best I've ever had. That I certainly cannot fault. My issue lies in the dessert and confusion with the staff at the time. I ordered the cheesecake. I started to eat it and realised it was still frozen in the middle, so I called the waiter over and explained this to him as best I could whilst demonstrating how frozen it was by pushing my spoon through the dessert. He said he would check with the kitchen staff. He then came back and took my plate away from me only to return with it a few minutes later and place the exact same dessert in front of me, half destroyed from my earlier demonstration to him. Pause now for awkward moment and a bit of a lost in translation moment, to which I took from his mumbled explanation to me that this was how the dessert was meant to be. Now I love cheesecake and never have I ever eaten a frozen one in a restaurant before. Not wanting to make any more of a scene I just decided to eat it, albeit working around the edges of the food until the middle was soft enough to eat enjoyably. I wish i had ordered the chocolate fondant which my girlfriend had and said was amazing!

Overall I would go back to this place but I certainly wouldn't order any cheesecake again.

Yummy pizzas at amazing value
Dec 2015 • Couples
We heard great reviews of this place and managed to score a table here without any reservations by arriving at 3.30pm in the afternoon. Best to book or come during off-peak hours if you do not have a reservation. The restaurant is not that easy to find and tucked down the end of a few little alleys. 

Pizzas were fresh and they are extremely generous with their toppings. Their burrata are made in-house and so fresh and creamy. We ordered 4 half-pizzas - magherita, prosciutto burrata, teriyaki chicken and 4 flowers. The 4 flowers pizza was the most unique with 4 types of real edible flower petals. Ordering the Buratta is a must as well! Do try their craft beers, we had one lemongrass flavoured beer and it was delicious.

Service was excellent and incredibly value-for-money for the quality and price paid.

The Best pizza in Saigon and in the world in my opinion
Jun 2015 • Friends
It's just an amazing and TERRIFIC place! It was my favourite place when I was living in Saigon and I was going there at least once a week! I could not get tired of it and among all my friends and the people I brought there, I don't know anyone who said he/she does not like it. This is a place you can't go if you do not have a booking beforehand unless you go after 9PM. Over the years, this place got so popular that it extended more and more its superficie! The food is just delicious, all the pizzas are amazing and you just love everything: it's tasty and fusion cuisine between Japanese and Italian. You normally go there with a bunch of friends and you all share pizzas, you can have half of a kind and half of another kind. The owners are super friendly, just one thing is that the waiters/waitresses at the time were not always fast and sometimes they got so busy that they often made mistakes in the orders. If you want, you also get the chance to sit next by the oven where you can actually see the staff making the pizzas and putting them in the oven. After living in Vietnam for 4 years, I had my last evening there and can't wait to go there again next time I travel to the city! just one word: AWESOME! I would recommend to anyone who visit Saigon even though I know it's weird to recommend pizzas to people who are travelling to Vietnam, but these are very special! I could go over and over again!

reviews.review_text:

13 contributions

Wow!!
Mar 2016
This has to be the best meal I've ever had not just in Saigon but anywhere. We lucked out the first time we tried to go to this place during a weekend dinner as it was completely booked and we would have had to wait an hour or more for a table. We tried the next day at lunch and got a table right away. You need to search for the place a bit but offline google maps directed us to the right spot. It's hidden in a residential alley between a takeaway dessert/coffee place and an Asian joint in a mall next to the alley.

The pizzas on the menu are distinctly a blend between Italian/American and Japanese. They do half-and-half pizzas which are great for people who would like to try different flavours/toppings in one meal. I chose their very popular Teryaki Chicken while my wife chose a basic Margharitta and neither of us regretted our choices. It was one of the yummiest pizzas we've ever had. The pastas on the other tables looked great too and if we were not stuffed we would have tried them out too. Service is top notch and prices are not really all that high for a joint that serves this high quality food. Everything tasted fresh, smelt great and had just the right amount of ingredients - base was just about right - not too thick/thin, not too crunchy/soggy, the cheese was very very fresh and just the right amount, the chilli oil they serve with the pizza was ablsoutely fantastic and added an awesome punch to the overall flavours. We'll be dreaming of these flavours for quite some time until the next time we eat something as memorable as these pizzas. The locals are fortunate to have a joint like this in their city.

On a side note, the 4Ps translates to some strange "Platform for Pizza for Peace...." which seemed like a weird name to make up to suit the acronym. But we could care less for what they call this place as long as they serve pizzas that are this good!

They were all amazing, seriously this was the best pizza I have ever had in my life. The pizza base was just perfect and none of it was at all greasy or oily like you sometimes get with pizza. They do half/half pizzas too so you can sample more! Service is very fast and there is free wifi. If you like pizza I would rate this place as a must do. Even if you don't like pizza you'll enjoy this (I normally won't eat it at home).
Tips to find it: it is a little hard to find as it is down an alley. There is a big blue "P" above the entrance to the alley like you're heading into a car park. The address is written 8/15 but that means unit 15 of number 8, as the numbers are written opposite to the west. It is near Sakyo Sushi and just near a Highlands Coffee.

They offer Teryaki chicken pizza, Japanese beef pizza, Salmon sashimi pizza and even dessert pizzas.

Great pizza by any standard
Dec 2015
Went in solo, was lucky enough to get a spot by the pizza oven. you dèinitely need reservations for bigger parties.

You can do half half pizza which was great. I normally rate my pizzas based on simple margherita pizzas, but this also gave me the opportunity to have the burrata which is really pricey at home and thus, an indulgence.

The pizza was great by western and Italian standard. Pizza is a personal choice, but I was quite impressed by the crust and quality of toppings. To be honest, I can't say that any pizza I have back home or in Italy is much better. It was a great pie.

The drink selection could do with a little bit more attention, with better choices by the glass - but what was available was decent. Unfortunately, they were not very flexible on substituting/adding ingredients (mushrooms) - but that's ok - it didn't take away from experience.

Sitting by the pizza station, I must say that I was particularly impressed with the quality control and system they had in place. This is not something I expected (at home, I am used to having one, maybe two guys man the pizza station). Everything was well organized here, and the owner/chef (?) was standing there supervising the food preparation and asked for employees to re do the food order if it wasn't up to his standard. On top of that, he would go around and serve the dishes to the patrons. That attention to details is important and I think this is well reflected in the food.

If you miss a taste from home, and want a break from vietnamese food as I did, this is a good place for families, dates and solo travellers!

Best Italian food in Asia
Dec 2015 • Solo
well... I know it's impossible to say this in fact is the best Italian food in Asia, but it is the best I've had, and I have been a place or two on this continent. 
First of all, it's a good idea to make reservations, because the place was packed both times I was there (yes I had to go back!). Anyway the staff will try to fit you in as soon as possible and provide with you with free water while you're waiting. So, to the most important... the food. I always say you should judge an Italian restaurant on two dishes: Spaghetti Bolognese and the Margarita Pizza. Basic Italian dishes, that can be exceptional if made correct. Both were excellent, especially the pizza. Second best Margarita pizza I've ever had.... brilliant tomato sauce... it was de-lish!!! The Bolognese had a nice twist with a light smokiness in the cheese.... a very nice surprise. Also had an appetizer and a dessert, both were great. Perfect Pizza

When you walk into the alley on 8 Lê Thánh Tôn, Pizza 4P will be on your left. 

Truth be told, I'm not even that big of a fan of pizza. But I came back four days in a row (not even ashamed of it. ...Okay, maybe a little bit). Their 4cheese pizza is heaven, and with the honey on the side it becomes... heaven with delicious honey on the side. You can choose two different pizza-flavors for each half if you want to, and besides the 4cheese, the pizza's with fresh burrata cheeses on them are also delicious. Legend goes that they learned how to bake pizza's via YouTube, and although I don't know if that is true, I'd say that they used one hell of a tutorial because this is definitely one of the best pizza's (if not THE best) I have ever eaten in my whole life. 

If you're there, try the coco+berry (or other coco+ xxx) drinks too, they're delicious. The desserts (that raspberry macarone... wow) are wonderful too, as are the salads and appetizers (cheese platter is excellent). 

Besides this, the service is thoughtful, attentive (water gets refilled promptly, genuine smiles), and professional. The decor is luxurious, authentic and hip. Prices are around 200.000 dong for a pizza, and very, very reasonable for everything that you get.

During my stay in HCMC I felt quite at home at this place and was happy to come here every time, and what was more, I always left being even happier! Please consider opening a shop in Amsterdam! ;)

Poor Service Good Concept
Sep 2015 • Friends
There are some cool ideas on their menu and in truth I would come back in a month or so just for the burrata, but the local hype really is not on par with the quality of the experience.

To start, the service was unprofessional, lazy, and all around dreadful. We booked a private room and found that no one came to check in on us for the first 30 minutes we were there as I eventually had to wander around the restaurant to find a waitress to bring us some drinks. Even when they did check in on us, we could easily tell the staff had about zero training as there attention to serving wine and other drinks was poor at best. This only compounded our woes as the wine menu was quite overpriced.

To boot, we found out through the local buzz online that none of their produce was from Da Lat as advertised. Not that it really matters as it would not be organic anyway, but why advertise a silly falsity like that anyway.

When it came to the food though, it was a bit of a roller coaster. Our salads were alright but nothing memorable. They had some nice appetizers however as everyone loved the camemberts on offer, but then our pasta course was once again rather plain and a bit lacking in substance. There were however some great pizzas as we all enjoyed the Japanese spin on the octopus pizza and we all enjoyed the burrata prosciutto pizza. But when we moved on to the desert course we just met more disappointment: an average tiramisu and some nasty frozen yogurt and chocolate ice cream that had been frozen and defrosted so many times that it had way too many ice crystals to be enjoyable.

Admittedly, with all the local hype and the need for reservations well in advance I grant you that our expectations were quite high and perhaps we should have privately known better but all around I would say that the experience was rather average.

Still, now knowing what I know, I would likely come back here every few months or better yet pick up some cheese for takeaway and may something more special in my kitchen at home.

Some of the best pizza i've had in Asia
Aug 2015 • Friends
Quick summary: must-visit if you like pizza!

Some of the best pizza you'll have in asia is...served in Saigon at an establishment opened by a Japanese expat (truly a wonder given that pizza in Japan generally starts at underwhelming - for example, without cheese - and goes downhill from there).

We arrived at lunch and the only places remaining were right in front of the pizza kitchen and (wood-burning) oven, which turned out to be great luck for us as we got to watch the cooking techniques, such as the kneading of dough balls. What immediately stuck out is the level of care taken at every stage of preparations- the temperature of the oven is monitored almost obsessively, the crust checked for thickness/tearing, fresh ingredients brought out individually for each pizza, etc. and the excellent results clearly bear out this level of care. The website and menu say that many of the cheeses are made fresh especially for them, and in general, the ingredients we saw being used were top rate.

They give you the option to order each pizza as half and half (of a type) rather than a full pie, and we took advantage of this, ordering 4 varieties on 2 pizzas - it seemed to work suprisingly well. We got a variety of the vegetarian options, all were good but our definite favourite was the aubergine. The one made from flowers was quite interesting too - kudos to the chefs for being so adventurous.

The atmosphere was elegant, being well balanced between casual and refined dining. Service was very good. A variety of different seating is available. Overall very much worth a visit.

Get directions first!
Apr 2015 • Couples
It's such a funny story how we found this place. It took us most of the afternoon to walk from Le Loi and Dhong Koi street before reaching this place. Le Thanh Ton street is long! So before walking it, make sure you know where it is. It's in what looks like the Japanese town of HCMC. It was surrounded with Jap restaurants abound. Oh, and if you don't know how to read Viet addresses by this time 8/15 means that it is WITHIN that alley. Once you've reached 8 Le Thanh Ton, GO IN THE ALLEY. They alley is in between 8 Le Thanh Ton and this big commercial building. You can ask the guard at the corner, he knows where Pizza 4P's is. Then turn left once you walk up the alley. (It's a short walk going up). Pizza 4P's is the furthest stall once you turned left. Hope that helps!

Once inside, it was so posh you'd forget that you walked all that way to work up a sweat. Haha. I loved that we looked so "summer casual" with our sleeveless tops and shorts against everyone else in the restaurant who was wearing, smart casual. But we were tourists so we didn't mind how others looked. Lol.

Get them to talk about their cheese! All the cheese is homemade and from scratch! So, they're proud of their cheese. They have a small section of history on their menu, you could read that up to know more about why Pizza 4P's is special in their own way. We ordered half/half of 2 pizzas (cuz we can), and a pasta dish. We were so famished that when the food came in, we just devoured them all! Oh, and the cheese? Tasted so good. Get their best sellers! We did!

Since it's a bit far off from the center, I suggest getting a cab to get back to your walking tour of HCMC center. :)

SAY CHEESE!
Jun 2015 • Solo
Squeezing into the tiny restaurant I was not immediately impressed with the surroundings as the location is not prime, nor is the interior design. However, I was quickly won over by the high quality staff: service was with a noticeably present smile and friendliness, hard to find in HCMC, and with a seriousness in their approach. Although it is a casual dining restaurant, the good service training comes through loudly: knowledge of the menu and product, upselling without being obnoxious, and attentiveness without being intrusive.

The CHEESE. That's the secret ingredient here. Very impressed with the range and quality of cheeses that these artisans make in Vietnam. The burata can hold its own against any from Wholefoods etc...obviously the quality of the milk, supposedly from Dalat, is very high.

The pizza itself is very well done. Observing the method and care of the pizza chefs, to the end product, this ranks as one of the best pizza's I've had. As a benchmark, for example taking the Brooklyn style Motorino's in HK (which I like a lot), 4Ps does it at least as good. The pizza dough is flavorsome and you wouldn't want to leave a bit of crust uneaten. It has less char, but plenty crunchy enough.

The toppings, though, are much more creative than Motorinos, and takes advantage of local produce. The four flowers vegetarian pizza was absolutely delicious, as was the burrata prosciutto pie, with the prosciutto generously laid out like a large rose on the pizza. 

I will definitely be back for more, and this is from someone who really wants to minimize on the carb intake!

Watch your time carefully!
Jun 2015 • Friends
We made a reservation for 6pm on a Monday. We made the reservation earlier on the day itself, and was told that the table was available but we could only have the table until 7.30pm. Although I'm always a bit turned off by restaurants that impose time limits to their patrons, I decided to still give this place a try since there are so many good reviews about it. 
We arrived late, at slightly before 6.30pm ( the taxi driver dropped us at the wrong place, and we had to walk around about 10mins to find our way). Before ushering us to our table, the waiter "remind" us again about the time limit, and tell us that we can only have the table until 7.30pm. Looks like they did not care that we arrived late, so now we only have 1 hour to have our meal. 
We sit down and ordered our meal. Food came pretty quickly. Salami and prosciutto with burrata cheese pizza is good, the pizza crust is nice and chewy (not a fan of thin crust pizzas). We also tried the Crab pasta, as recommended by our Vietnamese friend. 
Halfway through our meal, just before 7pm, a waitress come to our table asking us whether we would like to order anything else, which I find is rather weird because restaurants don't normally interrupt people during their meal and asked whether we wanted to order some more, do they? It may be ok if we have finished all our food, and they offered us dessert or something. 
Well, it might be just a polite way to say "Hey your time is almost up, if you want to order more, do so now, otherwise quickly wrap up and leave". 
We told the waiter that we've had enough food. So she left us alone, and we continued with our meal. Moments later (maybe 10-15min later) another waitress come over to our table and ask us the same thing. By then we had just finished our food and was enjoying our drinks and chit chatting. We said we won't order anything else, but did not asked for the bill yet, because we had not finished our drinks. 
And as the time limit is almost up, the waiter was left with no choice but to come over to our table again, probably determined to get us going as soon as possible. So we asked for the bill and left. 
Seriously, I understand that the restaurant is popular, and they might have another reservation at 7.30pm. But they certainly do not need to come over to our table 3 times interrupting our meal, and remind us about the time limit 2 times before we even sit down. It made us feel uneasy, as if we are being continuously watched over, and we were unable fully enjoy the meal. 
For such a popular and supposedly upscale restaurant, service is definitely disappointing. Maybe if you want to enjoy your pizza at your own pace, just take away.

After reading all the reviews backed up by local friends I had to give this place a go. I'm a pizza lover and rather critical when it comes to rating a pizza but here we go. Great first impression after arrival. Highly professional and positive waiters. Very tasteful Interior and ambience. Never Disappoints! But RESERVE early!
Apr 2015 • Friends
I've been going to 4P's since it opened a few years ago, and I cannot say that I've ever had a bad meal there. It's one of the most consistently great restaurants in town, and I'm always so happy when I leave. Every dish I've tried is delicious, but of course - I have my favorites.

Highly recommend starting with a garden salad & herb dressing. It's incredibly simple, but full of fresh flavor - and a perfect start before digging into pizza. It's difficult to pick a favorite pizza, but I would always recommend the fresh Burrata, Prosciutto and Rocket pizza. It's always a favorite with group dinners - but go earlier as sometimes they run out of the burrata or rocket (in which case, I recommend the salmon or 4-cheese pizzas). 

Service is always good. Staff isn't overly-friendly, but they are efficient and professional, which I like. Tables here go fast. I've never been successful reserving a table for dinner on the morning of, so I recommend calling a day before; otherwise, you just have to show up around 9pm and hope there's some space. If you go for lunch, I don't think reservations are as necessary - I've never had a problem getting a table at this time. 

My only hope is that they start to offer a better beer selection. They used to carry Chimay, but haven't had it the past few times I've been. It would be nice to see some of the new local craft beers on the menu too.

For me, 4P's certainly lives up to its reputation in town. I've never been disappointed in my meal there, and I can't wait until my next visit!

My boyfriend reserved a table at this restaurant after reading about it in an in flight magazine. We both went together. I was thoroughly satisfied with my half and half pizza. Sorry i cant remember the pizza titles...but it was a palatte tingling conversation stopping delight.

(Note: no other pizza restaurant we have visited in Vietnam stocks rocket. We have visited many. Apparently it's not cool enough in the evenings to grow it here. One supplier in Saigon grows it but only sells in large bulk)

My boyfriend was really looking forward to the experience, here is his review:

I ordered a prosciutto crudo (parma ham, arugula/rocket, flakes of parmesan with an extra tennis ball of house speciality cheese). 
What I received had virtually no sign of rocket (it was under the mozzarella) the tennis ball was missing, and there were no parmesan shavings. I asked the waiter for extra fresh rocket which was promptly delivered and I grabbed the full handful and demonstrated that there was only sufficient to cover half the pizza. I then requested the same amount again. I also pointed out the tennis ball of cheese was missing along with the parmesan. The tennis ball was delivered along with the second helping of rocket although the parmesan came in powder form rather than shavings. 
All my requests were dealt with promptly, politely and apologetically no matter how petty they seemed. 
Once everything was in place the only real let down was the parmesan powder. Upon breaking into the tennis ball soft cheese the creamy liquid centre was revealed and spread across the centre of the pizza by the waitress. After the first mouthful, all previous problems paled into insignificance.
The reviews I had read about the tennis ball cheese had proved to be true. You cannot buy a pizza with this cheese on anywhere else in the world to the best of my knowledge. 
It was the stuff dreams are made of.

I visited this out of the way café with a friend who was a previous very satisfied diner.

From experience, it was wise to make a booking a couple of hours before the required time of arrival. And it is just as well, because the place was fully occupied, as is often the case.

The taxi lets us off on the main street and directs us to take a short walk down the pedestrian only, lane. It is well lit and there are attractive businesses on both sides of the cheery walkway.

On entering the dining area, it is a pleasant surprise to notice that the tables are set with chairs that have arms. I like nothing better than to sit back and curl up into chairs with arms - especially after completing my meal.

There were four of us, so we selected a balanced range of pizzas. Yummo. The cheese is from their own farm in Da Lat.
The distinctive flavour was the result of Italian food prepared with a Japanese touch and Vietnamese ingredients. Delicious.

It is one of those places that is noted to be re-visited. And that is on the score of the pizzas, alone.
They do have pastas and starters etc to round off the meal.

And the excellent range of wines would suit any palate and every budget. We were impressed with the French range and chose a cabernet sauvignon which convinced us it was worth ordering a second bottle - especially at that bargain price! Of course there also, were name brand wines, at a reasonable price.

I was fascinated by the fit-out of the restaurant. It has ceramic tiles on the floor, a cement rendered ceiling and mini ceramic tiles on the large structural concrete columns. I immediately thought that would not be good for acoustics? And there was a floor to ceiling solid glass screen, which divided the dining area in two equal areas? Besides the full glass frontage? And no carpets or heavy drapes or anything to deaden noise?

I am not an interior decorator, but there was no people noise and the colour scheme and fit-out was very calming and created a very pleasant dining environment. It was noteworthy that all diners enjoyed their meals and conversations in appropriate tones. In fact, this is the first time I have been to a busy restaurant, anywhere in the world, where there was not one noisy table!

A great dining experience with wholesome and tasty food at a not expensive price, with attentive and cheerful service. It is definitely a place that will win repeat visits from their very happy customers.
