One of the best pizzas I've ever had
Mar 2015 • Family
I've eaten a lot of pizza in my days...Chicago style, New York thin crust, Pizza Hut, Korean pizzas with corn. But this. This was amazing. Hands down one of the best pizzas I've had. We got the signature Burrata Prosciutto Pizza that has: House-made burrata cheese, Prosciutto, rocket, fresh tomato, parmesan and olive oil.

It's cooked with the olive oil, parmesan, and garlic (if requested) crust in the wood stove. Then they top it afterwards with the rocket, tomato, and prosciutto and put a ball of their fresh burrata cheese on top. At the table, they cut into the cheese and it either oozes out (if hot enough), or is cut and laid out onto the 6 slices of pizza. 

I have experience with Pizza 4ps home delivery for their fresh produce and dairy products and as eager to try their restaurant, being very pleased with the quality and taste of what they've delivered to my house. It was no mistake to visit, only perhaps to not try it sooner! 

I would 100% recommend their specialty with burrata on top. It's unique and delicious. Cost is about 240.000 VND for one pizza. 

We also tried the "sushi" (ok, would not order again), the cheese fondue (excellent and worth ordering again, but not nearly enough items given to dip in the cheese), and another pizza that had tomato sauce that made the crust rather wet and soggy. I wouldn't order that one again. We ended the meal with the raspberry and rambutan macaroon which was beyond amazing. It was very, very hard to share with others as it after I took the first bite.

Oh, my husband had the cafe suada and said it was one of the best he's had in Saigon. We drink a lot of coffee...so high praise. 

Good service, great food, and we will definitely be back and recommend it to others.

Special Occasions, or any day.
Nov 2014 • Family
4P's Pizza is among the best restaurants I have been to. In addition to a wonderful selection of pizzas, many of which are unique to the restaurant, the look and feel of the restaurant is warm and inviting. 

4P's is passionate about what they do. They make their own cheese in Da Lat, they train their staff well (including English lessons to help better serve customers), and keep their restaurant really clean. 

Although 4P's is not ideal for children, the staff are wonderful with kids. The most recent time that my family and I went it was for my birthday. My son, who is 3 years old, was so excited for the whole day to get to celebrate my birthday, that when supper time came, he was fell asleep on the taxi ride to 4P's. The staff was quick to accommodate, moving two chairs together to create a makeshift cot for my son to rest in. It was great that the staff recognized the problem, and found a solution immediately, without a request being made. 

Although there is lots to see and do in Ho Chi Minh City, I think that 4P's is a must go location. Make reservations in advance, since 4P's fills up fast.

When 4Ps first opened, I think many in Saigon were skeptical. Pizza... by Japanese guys? What?! But it was very quickly realised that these guys were no fad. They were exceptional and here to stay.

Quality is second to none. It is immediately obvious the attention to detail. They work closely with Japanese run farms in Dalat and use high quality, organic produce. They make their own (delicious) cheese. They care about the little things. This is what sets them apart.

The menu is big, perhaps bigger than it needs to be, but I've yet to taste anything I didn't like. For me, the Parma Ham Pizza with a gooey Burrata cheese spread over it is as close to heaven as anything you're likely to find here. But also rating highly are the 5 Cheese Pizza (with honey, of course!), Terriyaki Pizza, Okonmiyaki Pizza, and the nicely made pastas. I have yet to have room left to try any dessert, but I will get there, I promise.

In a city full of good restaurants, 4Ps is great. Better make a reservation.

Since then, without any advertisement except by word of mouth, they'd expanded to take over the entire corner of the alley and now includes outdoor seating upstairs. Even with the growth their service remains impeccable, and the pizza is still just as delicious even though their main chef Yoshikawa no longer cooks as often. 
I love their creative fusion style, merging Japanese and Vietnamese ingredient with Italian cuisine. Everything tastes great. I particularly love their green salad (with local herbs) and salmon sashimi pizza. Yum! Some of the pizzas here you will not find anywhere else.

Excellent service, excellent pizza!
Nov 2014 • Friends
Living in Vietnam and not being a fan of local food, I am constantly on the hunt for restaurants serving delicious Western food. A friend and I heard about 4 P's from a coworker and decided to check it out. The place is a bit difficult to find - our taxi driver dropped us off on the main road and motioned to us that it was down an alley we had parked next to. Thankfully, staff from another restaurant in that alley pointed us in the right direction!

First of all, it is highly recommended that you make a reservation. We did so, but ended up showing up a little early to escape the heat. This was not a problem, they were able to seat us immediately. From the outside, the restaurant looks very tiny, but once inside the restaurant seems to open up right before your eyes. Lots of places for couples to large groups! The decor is simple but beautiful, and from the moment we walked in the waitstaff were incredibly attentive.

The menu is robust in size with many options for starters, pastas, and of course - pizzas. They do not have different sizes of pizzas, just one (approximately 12" I suppose). Personally, I very highly recommend the five cheese pizza. It is served with a little container of honey, something I had never heard of, but when I poured the honey on top of the pizza I was astonished at how well the flavors combined. We also ordered the molton lava cake for dessert, and it was also very good.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience! I will absolutely be back on my next trip to HCMC.

Great Pizza
Jul 2014 • Friends
This Japanese owned Italian pizza and food restaurant was recommended by a friend when it was newly opened. Food is very balanced and you find the love, innovation and care in their food and ingredients. Even a copy cat was opened with exactly same menu but not up to the standard/originality. Call for reservation [several days] in advance is now a must for Pizza 4Ps especially for Thu-Sat evenings. Reservation would be best in Vietnamese as the name could be misspelled and mixed up. I like that pasta is not overcooked. However, pasta is sometimes served cold (or is this their style?).
 
The team is nice, and friendly chefs. Staff was very honest keeping my bag forgotten there, even overnight. Despite their good service, I think they still need to upgrade the professionalism and efficiency of staff given their fast growing business. I understand it's hard to find, train and keep good hospitality staff in Vietnam. I would also want a warmer service towards local customers or [skinny] customers who simply want 4Ps tasty pasta dishes than big meal. Regardless, I would highly recommend Pizza 4Ps for their love of perfection and in serving innovative dishes. 

This is the place you can have 2 types of pizza toppings in one (yummy teriyaki chicken!), vegetarian pizza, even sweet pizza (not sure if you're convinced but you'd be wowed just by checking it out!). Their breakfast menu is amazing as well. Saving the best for last: their chocolate dessert!!! 
Pizza 4Ps is tucked away in a small helm in the busy Japanese area in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, so you find some peace from the heavy traffic.
 
Pricing wise, it used to be more reasonable (for local standard). For Saigon standard, I would rate it 5* given limited choices of quality food and service, and value. I was here multiple times for different types of gatherings/meetings.

Went there countless time with friends, family and clients. 4P's of 3 years ago was a tiny restaurant hidden in an alley with tasty food and good customer service. 4P's today is just bad in every way possible. Every time I call them to book in advance, either they do not pick up, or the restaurant is fully booked. How is it possible for a restaurant to be fully booked 5 days earlier - unless they do not want more customers. I do understand that the restaurant is always crowded (although not 100% tables are occupied) and they can be content with how they are doing, but it is going down, way down. It can be wonderful experience for those who eat there the first time, especially the tourists, but this absolutely cannot be one of the top restaurants in Saigon. A couple examples: 1. My friends wanted pizzas and specifically the burrata prosciutto so we tried to call them to reserve a table. Called both numbers (a land line and a mobile) 5 times, no one picked it up. We decided to just walk in and there was a table for us. We noticed that the phone was in the "reception" area and it was ringing non stop but no one really cared to pick it up. 2. The carnations they used to put in the center table attracted a lot of blow flies and it was purely unhygienic to eat with flies flying around you. 3. My friend called 4 days in advance to book for a party of 15 and the guy on the phone said it was no table available unless he agreed to eat at 2 PM. My friend said he wanted to talk to a manager which he did, and suddenly a table was available for him. How? I can go on and on, but if the owners of 4P's read this, I notice you are not often present in the restaurant anymore. If you leave the restaurant to your staff who: do not know they can merge tables for a big company, do not know what kinds of cocktails there are on the menu, do not know that you do serve a pizza that is called 4 flowers; prefer to say "sorry we have no table available"; then it's guaranteed to be operation downfall.

Once, Twice, Three times DISAPPOINTED!!!!!!!!!!!
May 2014 • Business
I had heard a lot about this restaurant through friends and over the last month i have been to this restaurant 3 times! not through choice but twice because friends wanted to go there for dinner and the other time because i had a business meeting there for lunch. 

The first time i went there my friend and i arrived around 4.30pm for an early dinner. The restaurant was quite empty and the service was quick, i ordered the Tomato Spaghetti with Crab and Tomato Sauce. When my dish arrived it looked lovely, the crab was a good size and there was a lot of sauce over the pasta. The dish was divine!!!!! Plus cracking the crab claws was fun and getting the crab meat out made the meal more interesting. 

we ordered a dessert to share which was the lemon meringue pie, this was not good! it was served cold and you could tell that these are brought in from frozen! (i am a qualified chef). 

Then the following week i had business meeting to go to and they had arranged to meet at the 4ps for lunch as the business people. The restaurant was was not busy but the service was bad! we waited ages just to order drinks. i ordered the Crab again because it was so nice the first time - BIG MISTAKE. 

My dish arrived much later after every one else's in fact i had to ask the waiter where my meal was, When my dish finally arrived and i could tell it had been sitting in the kitchen for a while waiting for a waiter to bring it to me! 

The pasta was Luke warm, it looked smaller than the first time and there was hardly any sauce, when i asked for more sauce, the waitress didn't understand, i asked 3 different waitress for extra sauce and the answer i got was 'Sorry not understand you', i gave up! then i asked for some hot and i got the same answer. i was very disappointed with my meal, i advised the business people NOT to order dessert and we went some where else for home made dessert. 

Then a a week later it was my friends birthday and she wanted to go the 4ps, so i tried again, and i ordered the crab dish this arrived EVEN SMALLER. The crab was the SMALLEST crab i had ever seen and over cooked and the pasta was dry and hardly any sauce. 

Now this is where i get angry, for a restaurant to be GOOD it has to be consistent with the quality OF FOOD and food portions. The 4ps does not do that! i ordered the same dish 3 different times on 3 different occasions and every time the dish got smaller, dryer and more tasteless! 

The service seemed to get worse EVER TIME I WENT. There seems to be a lot waiting staffing but they don't do anything but stand there in their own little worlds and in the end i had to actually get up and ask for someone to come and serve US!!!!!!!!! 

Would i go back NO because this restaurant has proved to me that they DONT CARE about their standard of food! is it worth the money NO. There other restaurants that i have been to where the food and service is ALWAYS GREAT. THIS IS NOT ONE OF THEM!!!!!!!!!!!! 

As i have said in my other reviews i run an orphanage and i get asked by my many volunteers and visitors for recommendations of places to eat. would i recommend this place to my visitors and volunteers NO NO NO. 

The only thing i would say is if you like pizza's that have a different twist then i guess this is the place to go, but be ready for a long wait and don't go excepting great food as this place is hit and miss and i would say MORE MISS than anything!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Outstanding restaurant
Apr 2014 • Friends
We came here by word of mouth and all I can say is that it's a well deserved reputation. In case you miss food from home and want to do a small break on the pho and other Vietnamese specialities this is the perfect place to do so. I mean even home you'll struggle to find a place like Pizza 4p. The home made mozarella and buratta are incredible. All "à la carte" choices deserve hesitation as everything seem able to whet your appetite, and actually is. We appreciated the possibly of mixing half pizza so we had the chance to taste 5 different ones. The wine list is also worth a special mention. And the deserts... wow ! The chocolate fondant is in itself worth keeping some room in your stomach as you can't go without trying it really. Prices are not too steep considering the quality of this restaurant. I recommend it!

4P's Pizza:VERY BAD and POOR SERVICE!!! DISAPPOINTING!!!!
Apr 2014 • Solo
First and foremost, I like this restaurant because of great food taste especially their unique pizzas. BUT then, something has gone TERRIBLY WRONG when I dine in here last week.
I arrived at 11am on a weekend and it wasn’t crowded at all.

Originally, I wanted to have brunch or breakfast but because of the time, I just couldn’t. Secondly, I ordered ravioli pasta but then the staff said they COULDN’T MAKE IT NOW with no reason. He just told me that they can make it after 12noon. So thirdly, I had to change my order into CLAM PESTO PASTA. Settled. Rough 40 minutes later (11.40am), my order hasn’t arrived yet. I ask one of the staffs. 10minutes later STILL NOTHING. Another 10minutes of looong waiting, I followed-up my order again angrily and disappointingly. NOBODY confirm back to me about my SINGLE ORDER of PASTA. I was thinking of leaving the restaurant. I was so hungry and tummy was literally aching because of WAITING FOR SO LONG. Finally, after WAITING FOR EXACTLY 1HOUR OF ONE ORDER OF PASTA, it arrived. Of course, I was SO ANGRY and UPSET, VERY DISAPPOINTED and sooooo UNHAPPY with the service and everything.

Although the male owner did apologize but the DAMAGE HAS ALREADY BEEN DONE and this incident was never OK and NEVER WILL BE OK. That time wasn’t crowded at all. I can even cook 1KILO for PASTA for about 10 PERSONS for 20minutes to 30minutes. How about this UNPREPARED restaurant which opens at 7.00am for breakfast????!!!! I just found out also today from another friend that their SERVICE has really GONE BAD!

1 ORDER OF PASTA FOR ONE HOUR???!!!!! SERIOUSLY!!!! DON’T TELL ME IF I ORDER 1 LARGE PIZZA IT WILL TAKE 2HOURS; or 5 PASTAS FOR 5HOURS!!!!! MY GOD!!! WHAT A SHAME!!!!! IT’S A SHAME!!!!!!!

Pizza 4P's
Dear abcd w,

Thank you for giving us your honest feedback.
Regarding your last visit, we sincerely apologize about our poor service.

Due to the system error, your order wasn't sent to the kitchen and we also failed to check with the kitchen carefully enough. We are very sorry that you had to wait for your food for a long time and had an unpleasant experience because of our poor service. It's also our fault that we couldn't explain the situation thoroughly when it happened.

We've been training our staffs to provide a great dining experience to all of our guests.
And we have to prevent an issue like this no matter what. We are very sorry about it.
We take this incident very seriously and train our staffs to serve all of our customers better.
Thank you very much for giving us your feedback.

Also, we had a meeting with the restaurant manager about this issue today and discussed what exactly happened and how we can prevent it in the future.
We will talk to all the staffs and continue to improve our service to avoid the same mistake.
Again, thank you very much.

Best regards, 
Masuko, Owner of Pizza 4P's

Singapore85 contributions

Not your usual pizza
Feb 2014 • Friends
Neat little place that you won't expect to find in HCMC.
A little pretentious, due to a somewhat over-representation of a certain type of 'dating' couple, still there were enough local (expatriate) patrons for the place to be suitable for the more conservative diners. Be warned - it's noisy, as the tables are set very closely together. If you are here for a nice quiet conversation with your long lost friend, you would have better luck on whatsapp. The tables are close enough that you can reach over and pick up a slice from your neighbour.
The pizzas are ok - the half and halfs are quite interesting. It's not your usual hawaiian or all beef.
The cheese is quite good; get some to take back to the hotel if you are in HCMC for a couple of days.
Prices are relatively high, but then that's true of everything in HCMC, even food in the supermarket is expensive.

My favorite place in Saigon! you can experience delicious food, great service:)
Feb 2014 • Friends
Last February, I had traveled southeast asian countries with my friends.
We had traveled for a month so we bored same dishes and same service which many restaurants provide. Then, we did dined here. 

We tried fresh caprese, margherita pizza, 4 kinds of cheeses pizza, Burrata pizza along with pastas and desserts. We have never tried these great tastes in not only southeast asian countries but also Japan. It was special one!

Why could they provide these great dishes? Yosuke Masuco who are owner of Pizza4p's told us because they have used homemade cheese and fresh vegetables which are made in Da lat where is likes plateau. I think it is very difficult that other people imitate same ways in other restaurants which include Japanese and Europe.
We had wanted to eat again and went here the next day lol

I also want to introduce great service here because I think the condition of great restaurant is not only taste but also service. Staff introduced recommend dishes and drink for us who are not familiar with it. In fact, one of the staff talked about details of dishes for us every times. she is very kind and nice smile so we spent good time! I appreciate her. 

I wanan go here when my next trip in Saigon:) and if you have a chance coming Saigon, I highly recommend Pizza4p's!!!

All about Pizza 4 P's incredible food quality has been mentioned in my previous review. This time I would love to tell you a story about how amazing their staffs are. 

Nov 11 I decided to order a half magherita - half quattro formaggi for pick up. As usually, I was greeted with the nicest answers and best manner over the phone - and then had a lovely little surprise being told that my pizza would be ready "in 10 minutes" - that's crazily fast - I rarely had my food ready in 10 mins, especially with pick up orders @___@ 

When I arrived at the place to pick up (5-7 minutes or so after the call), I was asked to take a seat while they packed the pizza for me. As spontaneous as I could be, I decided to dine in instead of taking away and eating alone by myself at the hotel. It was around 9:00pm, the place was no longer as packed as it is usually at 7-8pm, I always loved P4Ps interior, and the bar has a few spare seats.

Sep 2013 • Family
Heard so much about this place and it did live up to all the great reviews it got from my friends and family.

Located in a cul-de-sac, unusual street for a restaurant or any kind of other businesses, you walk up to this clean, modern-looking, hidden gem restaurant whose outstanding pizzas consist of a fusion of Japanese and Italian cuisines.

Everything in this restaurant seemed to mesh well. From the décor, to the energetic atmosphere, to the professionalism of the waitering services, to the creative menu. 

We had the salmon sashimi pizza, along with the teriyaki chicken and the burrata prosciutto pizza which were all full of flavors. The salads were very good as well, with either a balsamic vinaigrette or a pesto sauce option.

We finished it off with a dessert pizza: ½ apple and the other half strawberries.

Loved the fact that you have the option to do one half of the pizza one way, and the other another way.

This is a restaurant that I would definitely recommend on your next visit to Ho Chi Minh as myself, I would make sure to not eat any carbs a few days before so that I can indulge myself in all the delicious dishes that this place has to offer.

The only thing that I would have preferred is a crushier pizza crust. But the good balance of the toppings and the creativity behind them made up for it.

This is an amazing fusion of Japanese and Italian cuisines that you should not miss!

So we sat there waiting like we were told to and we were pretty much invisible there. 

Meanwhile, two Japanese gentlemen came in a few minutes after us and they were greeted cheerfully. They also get served water, knives, forks and their menu brought to their table. Me and my friend witnessed all of this as the staff walked pass us (we sat in the table opposite to the door so we're obviously closer to the staff than them, funny enough). So we asked the menu and the waitress brought them to our table (we already chose this table by this time since there's no more spot). Still, there's no water so we had to ask for them again and each of us got a different cup. 

First we ordered the pizza Okonomiyaki. After that, me and my friend made a joke about how will we would get our food later than the other two Japanese gentlemen even though we ordered first. But almighty God, we actually got ours first! That's the good news, the bad news is it it was dead cold. (Oh and by the way we still had to ask for knives and forks since there as nothing on the table) I was about to ask to talk to the manager here about this but my friend didnt want that and we were both too hungry so we just ate it. It was decent, nothing amazing like I've heard. Perhaps if we get the normal version which should be warmer then it should help with the taste. I mean like come on, even the $1 food I ate in the street are served hot.

Still, we decided to be patient with 4P since we have heard rave things about the tiramisu here. It was good but $4 for a small one = not a good value for me. After that, we asked for our bill, paid and went to the little Floramisu shop next door for a much better experience.

Another thing to note is that me and my friend kept chuckling and making jokes about the service here so we might looked like idiots a little bit. Hence, they might actually took us as idiots and served us like so. (The staff actually saw us like that and they seemed to have a negative reaction to it)

To sum up, if we were to go to 4p or you as a local Vietnamese, we should definitely go with a foreigner. Or dress up like one, speak English, Japanese or whatever it takes so that we wont get this kind of "special" treatment. Hope that this isnt actually a part of their training program to automatically value foreign customers over local customers.

Hope that this isnt too long to read. I typed it with a mood. Granted, I rarely spend my time doing these things but with a case where you have much expectation and receive even great disappointment like this, I guess it's worth it.

4P's Pizza - Japanese & Italian fusion, delicately prepared coal oven baked Pizzas. 4P's is more than a Pizza place. It has the best 'homemade' mozzarella cheese I have ever tasted. Solid Pizza and Pasta - Tips on how to find Pizza 4P
Jan 2013 • Couples
A bit of an escape from local food located in an alley that can be a bit challenging to find, Pizza 4P delivers a great pizza and pasta experience with a really nice staff in a small location. 

You have to have the true wood fired pizza if you are going to go here -- and for the experience, you can book the pizza bar where you can watch yours (as well as all the other) pizzas being made and baked. A true wood burning oven that must be extremely hot, we timed the pizzas and they were cooking for about 100 seconds! 

Tips on Pizza 4P

1) Get a reservation -- this place is not too large, and a reservation is HIGHLY recommended. It fills up quickly. 

2) Finding Pizza 4P. We were a bit challenged on finding it because it is off the main street in an alley. Located off of Le Thanh Tong road, you want to be on the side of the road with the (apparently) new Domino's pizza place (a bit of an odd coincidence, but trust me, don't even think about Domino's over Pizza 4P). If you are walking on Le Thanh Tong street and the Domino's is on your RIGHT, then go past it, and turn RIGHT on the alley IMMEDIATELY adjacent to the Domino's. Go to the end, and turn LEFT at the “T” in the alley. Pizza 4 P will be at the end of the alley on your left hand side.

Obviously, if you are coming up Le Thanh Tong road and the Domino’s Pizza is on your LEFT hand side, turn LEFT up the alley immediately BEFORE Domino’s, go to the end, turn LEFT again, and Pizza 4P will be on your left at the end. 

3) If you have an interest in watching pizzas being made, you can book a seat (or several seats, I think you can fit six -- notice the word “table” is missing here) at the pizza bar. I am not certain what the restaurant calls it, but it is up close and personal with the making of pizzas and wood burning oven. (See photo attached to this posting). We did this one evening and had fun watching, as well as met another couple who sat next to us. A more casual experience than sitting at the tables, and we recommend it if you have this type of interest. 

4) The pasta is very well done, and as good as the pizzas. 

We found the service to be extremely friendly and nice...although they were a bit rushed at times. No communication issues, and we highly recommend going here if you are seeking Italian in Viet Nam.

In a part of the world, where Italian cuisine in general, and gourmet pizza in particular, are as alien as common sense in the Republican Party, this place has supposedly the pizza in Vietnam. After spending over a week here, I would not be surprised with this statement.

This is a small place tucked at the back of an alley where you need to make reservations even to hold your spot at the bar. Yes, it is wildly popular, and deservedly so. The pizza was gourmet alright, with an excellent crust, perfect mozzarella, fresh basil, but the tomato sauce was a bit off. The size was just right for an individual person, it came piping hot from the wood fired oven, had the wonderful charred taste of the wood, and was almost perfect. However, there is one major problem. The pizza choices are very limited, and the vegetarian choices are just two, of which they ran out of the mushrooms, so we were stuck with just the margarita. I ordered the spaghetti caprese as well. The description said it had anchovy oil which I found very disconcerting in an Italian place. I ordered it without the anchovy oil, and the dish was barely tolerable. Stick with the margarita and mushroom pizzas, and you will be fine. They also have an interesting selection of wines at very reasonable prices.

Our waiter was a very pleasant fellow, and at the end when I started chatting with him, he turned out to be the owner! Go for it!

- Prosciutto pizza, topped with plenty of arugula and (wait for it) prosciutto! Did not skimp = a very happy me.

- Four flowers pizza, very fresh, and would make any veggie lover happy.

Yes, it's more expensive than a typical meal you can get in HCM. Yes, it was totally worth going out of your way for. Yes, I'm coming back because I watch them make their house special pizza topped with prosciutto, arugula, AND burrata cheese! (No halfies on this one... don't care, I'm getting my own).

Italian Pizza with a Japanese twist
Dec 2012 • Couples
I read the reviews on TA and wanted to find what some call the best pizza in HCMC. They have a large selection of pizza 20 various selections. Some of the choices are new to me and I have been eating pizza for many years. I will comment on the two pizzas I had. The pizzas are cooked in a wood fired oven just like they are in Naples, Italy which in I have had the best pizza ever. Better even than the Mom and Pop pizza places in the North east of the US. The best seating in the restaurant are in front of the oven where the Japanese chef prepares the pizzas. I found it to be comfortable and not hot at all. For starters I would recommend the Green salad with herbs and homemade dressing this is for sharing. Skip the clam chowder not worth it. Better chowder available in HCMC. For Pizza selection go with the simple Marinara this is the best pizza I have had in HCMC. It was fantastic prepared perfectly. You will not be disappointed in this selection. It is simple crust, sauce and garlic with no other toppings. It is very light and one pizza per person is what I recommend. The Margherita pizza is just okay and I would not order again it is a typical pizza in any place around town. I would also skip the tomato spaghetti with house made sauce again average rating. Desert is also top notch I would recommend the fondant chocolate cake as well as the Hiromil’s creamy tiramisu which is surprising as I normally do not like tiramisu but here it is delicious. The house wine both the red and the white are good and recommended. So again go with the green salad, Marina pizza and the deserts with a carafe of your choice of wine and you will not be disappointed. I would recommend making a reservation as it is a busy place.

Worthwhile experience
Aug 2012 • Friends
Working in ho chi Minh city for almost a year makes me understand the hidden gems terms about the restaurants and cafe here, which mostly not strategically placed in heart of busy area, or across the big street.
4P pizza is one of those. Situated not across the big street, we have to made extra effort to reach the restaurant, through the small inclined alley, and waited for 30 min ( reservation in advanced is a most!) and.. Voila, we entered very cozy and comfy restaurant, with friendly staff and pizza cooking scent which totally giving the whole atmosphere in that place very different. They have huge pizza oven in the middle of the restaurant, hence we could see how the pizza made.
We ordered 1 cheese pan and 1/2 pan of flower pizza and 1/2 pan of chicken teriyaki. We were so curious about the flower pizza as we never had it before. It tools only 8 min, and our order arrived, it was taste so delicious! I never had pizza like this before, and these pizza (especially the flower pizza) is the best I ever taste in my life..
After amazing pizza we close the dinner with lemongrass tea, chocolate fondant and tiramisu. It's a bit difficult to find nice desert in ho chi Minh city, so we werent put so much hope on it, but it's totally changed our perception that we got the chocolate fondant perfectly cooked, and the tiramisu is very yummy. Last is the lemongrass tea... It's very fresh and genuine.
All in all, it was amazing experience, and truly worthwhile after the long walk and wait. We will definitely come back again, either for the pizza, or the yummy dessert, or the coffee and authentic tea!

Not bad but poor environment, no soul
Jul 2012 • Solo
I went to try Pizza 4P's for lunch based on recent good reviews in Tripadvisor.
For those looking for italian restaurant, this isn't one. I hadn't read comments so I discovered upon arrival, since the restaurant is located in a hidden alley between Le Thanh Ton & Ly Tu Trong.
The mini dining room was full so I was taken by the gentle waitress to 1st floor of the dessert shop next door. This is a dark silent room, so don't expect lively environment.
The atmosphere is ... well, Japanese. Having lived in the area years ago, I quite know about the dominant population living around.
It's just not my cup of tea to eat pizza in a dead environment.
Regarding the food, I must say that it was quite good. It's italo-japanese pizza. They allow you to order to 1/2 pizzas, so that you can have 2 different types in one. I had 1/2 tuna curry and 1/2 quattro flowers.
It's so frequent to be bored of pizza after 2 slices because it's dry and flavourful that I want to insist that it's not the case here. I loved what I ate, no matter whether it's italian or fusion.

So I may say go for the food (I guess other dishes are of good quality too), not for the atmosphere, unless you fancy "very confidential" one.

There was sth special on my day, a model photo shooting in the dining room, which had little or nothing to do with the restaurant itself. Well, the model girl was pleasant to watch, so no objection. Just a bit surprising :) This is Vietnam also.

4P's pizza took some finding - its down a lane way, and around a corner (the lane way runs next to dominos pizza - don't stop there!). But we were determined and on a rainy friday night we found it.

We hadn't booked, and the place was packed - and despite the best efforts of the staff, they didn't have a spare table. 

I guess we looked a little downhearted, so the waiter offered to set us up in the cafe next door (i think it might be owned by the same people - there were just some people having drinks there). So we got to eat some fantastic wood fired pizza at the cafe next-door to 4P's!

Japanese style Pizza - yummy
Mar 2012
Ever heard of a Japanese Pizza Restaurant? No? Me neither, until last night when we where looking for some non-Asian option. And we found Pizza 4Ps on tripadvisor. The place is kind of hidden at the end of a small road. We arrived without a reservation and were asked to wait and they will see what they can do for us. A few minutes later they came back and told us that only two places at the Pizza bar are available and that it is kind of small and hot. We were shortly thinking about the offer and as we were hungry decided to take it. And it was a very good decision to do so. The Pizza bar is just the best place in this restaurant - it's opposite of the Pizza chef and his team and the big wooden oven - yes, it's wooden - something you do not find that often any more even in Italy. We ordered two very different kind of Pizzas. The classic Margarita with fresh basil and an SRP. SRP means more or less shrimps with cheese. Both were delicious and had the real Pizza taste. Crusty and they even use mozzarella and not this kind of artificial Pizza cheese. The Japanese team is very friendly and quick.They even explained that they can only deliver one Pizza at the time and hoped that it wouldn't be a problem for us. If you want to start eating together you can even go for the half-half option. Which basically means that you get two different Pizzas on one. You can even do it if you feel one full Pizza would be too much. As I did not have any other Pizza in Vietnam so far I cannot say if this one is the best in Vietnam, but I would say that it is great and even better than many Pizzas I had on many other places on this globe, even Italy. Go for it and try it out.

The two meals I had at this restaurant convinced me to get a tripadvisor account just so I could rate and trumpet this place from the rooftops. I am a pizza snob. I am the kind of person who decides after one meal at a pizzeria called Dar Poeta to study abroad for a semester in Rome largely so I can eat well, then comes back to the states and doesn't eat any for months because nothing at home compares. I guess I don't need to mention so much about their famous mozzarella cheese. 
They are homemade, and you should know the effort they put in to make these gorgeous mozzarella. So when you go to this restaurant, please try any dish with mozzarella cheese, including pizza.

Last but not least, I had their famous pizzas. Pizza Margherita is the delicacy you must try in this restaurant. Not only the perfect combination of their famous homemade mozzarella and fresh tomatoes, but you should also see how the pizzas are made. 
The chef (trained in Japan) will make every pizza one by one and cook it in the oven.

The services are very good, and staffs are all very friendly. The atmosphere is soooo cozy. 

It might be a bit difficult to find the place because you have to walk a short distance back from the main road (So don't forget to print out a Map and take memo of contact number just in case!!!!)

I would rather have kept this place silent, like a secret garden but I have decided not to be selfish this time, and I WOULD ABSOLUTELY RECOMMAND THIS RESTAURANT.

Alas! Found the BEST PIZZA IN HCMC!!!!
Jul 2011
After having wasted so many visits to Pizza places, at last, I have found the go to place for Pizzas in HCMC.

This place with a very nice and cool interior seems to be owned by Japanese, but the Pizza they provided was very very authentic (for the authentic ones like Pizza Margherita or Quattro Formaggio). Price of pizzas ranges from below 100,000 VND to around 300,000 VND.

The crust of the pizza has a fabulous savory scent which probably derives from the wood-fired oven, and is rather thick on the edge, and a little thin toward the inside - complete Naples style pizza. It is crispy and at the same time it has a chewy texture, which is so difficult to resist. Especially the Magherita that we had was so good with the beatiful scent of the Mozzarella cheese. I was also very surprised when the staff mentioned that the Mozzarella cheese was home made.

There were intersting Japanese type pizzas such as Teriyaki or Mayonaise shrimp, and also pizzas with a Vietnamese feature, such as Four Flower Pizza. I will definitely try the Four Flower Pizza next time.

The wine list was decent with around 10 bottles each for red and white, and was actually on the cheap side starting from the 300,000 VND zone compared to other restaurants serving the same kind of wines. Personally interested in the Aile d' Argent, since it was the first time I saw this one in Vietnam.

The service was also very nice and attentive. Sometimes it took time for the pizzas to come, but looking at how the Pizzaiolo bakes its pizza (he doesn't just stick in bunch of pizzas in the oven, and he seemed so careful about how he bakes the pizzas), we might have to wait to be able to enjoy this carefully made pizzas. 

I would say the best seat would be right in front of the oven, although it might be a bit hot. You know that Pizzas are at their best when they are just baked.
